hints: Use logarithm laws to expand $\ln(p/q) = \ln p - \ln q = a$ and $\ln(q^2p) = \ln p + 2\ln q = b$.
Solve this linear system of two equations for $\ln p$ and $\ln q$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.
Substitute your expressions into $\ln(p^7q) = 7\ln p + \ln q$.
walkthrough:
Apply logarithm laws to express the given equations as a linear system in $\ln p$ and $\ln q$:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{p}{q}\right) = \ln p - \ln q = a \quad [1]$$
$$\ln(q^2 p) = \ln p + \ln(q^2) = \ln p + 2\ln q = b \quad [2]$$

Subtract equation [1] from equation [2] to eliminate $\ln p$ and solve for $\ln q$:
$$(\ln p + 2\ln q) - (\ln p - \ln q) = b - a$$
$$3\ln q = b - a \implies \ln q = \dfrac{b - a}{3}$$

Substitute $\ln q$ into equation [1] to solve for $\ln p$:
$$\ln p = a + \ln q = a + \dfrac{b - a}{3} = \dfrac{3a + b - a}{3} = \dfrac{2a + b}{3}$$

Expand $\ln(p^7 q)$ using the power and product laws of logarithms:
$$\ln(p^7 q) = \ln(p^7) + \ln q = 7\ln p + \ln q$$

Substitute the expressions for $\ln p$ and $\ln q$ into this expansion:
$$\ln(p^7 q) = 7\left(\dfrac{2a + b}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{b - a}{3}\right)$$
$$= \dfrac{7(2a + b) + (b - a)}{3} = \dfrac{14a + 7b + b - a}{3}$$
$$= \dfrac{13a + 8b}{3}$$
